findings.status_label_authority: owner ruling 2026-08-21. This finding is a provenance/reproducibility defect and is NOT evidence of numerical drift — but it is also NOT declared globally non-blocking. Both halves of the label are load-bearing and must be quoted together.

findings.title: The bound dependency-bundle content identity cannot be reproduced by any tooling in the repository.
findings.statement: The bound value 26e230493f218aba332b0888f2751def9f143ee136f68a86bdb91aaa03110dc1 was not reproduced by any of NINETEEN candidate canonicalisations computed inside the bound container over the mounted bundle: two-space hash-path lines (the format mr002_v2_tree_aggregate.py uses), one-space, path-then-hash, hashes-only, streaming rel+bytes, streaming bytes-only, hash-lines, JSON dict (indented and compact), NUL-separated, rel=hash, raw-digest concatenation, sorted-by-hash, tab-separated, no-newline, walk-order variants of two of these, absolute-path, and basename-only. The file COUNT matches the record exactly (2954), and the mount demonstrably happened, so this is a lost-algorithm problem and not evidence that the bundle drifted.
findings.precedent: This is the same failure class the repository already documents. apps/backend/scripts/mr002_v2_tree_aggregate.py records that the prior rollback aggregate ff0308be99dd82087b03ef3b48006f4a7c4b87ca37bd951a8be42794c03f4bbc 'was computed on the host under an implementation that is not preserved anywhere in this repository' and that 'seven plausible formula variants over two candidate file sets ... all failed to reproduce it.' That docstring states the general lesson: 'an aggregate described in prose and re-implemented twice is two algorithms wearing one name.' The deps-bundle identity is a second instance of exactly that.
findings.proportionate_assessment: This does NOT impugn numerical determinism. Every numerical library — numpy, scipy, quadprog, piqp, mpmath, clarabel — resolves from the IMAGE, and the image config digest matches the bound value exactly. The unverifiable bundle supplies pyarrow and the AWS/dateutil libraries, none of which participate in solving a QP or evaluating a certificate.
findings.recommendation: A future freeze must bind the dependency bundle with an identity produced by a SHIPPED, versioned implementation, on the same footing as mr002_v2_tree_aggregate.py. Recording a hash without preserving the function that produced it yields a value that can be quoted but never checked. Do NOT retrofit a new algorithm onto the old number and call it verified.

findings.title: The development corpus cannot be reproduced on this host as provisioned.
findings.statement: corpus.npz is not present in the bound tree (/opt/mr002/phase3c_src/.mr002out does not exist), and /opt/mr002/inputs contains only Validation-2 material — config.json, sessions.json, structural_manifest.json, reference_manifest.json, upload_manifest.json. This host was provisioned as a VALIDATION execution host. The development dataset that mr002_n1_capture_corpus.py replays over the window 2013-01-02 to 2019-10-02 is not on it.
findings.why_it_matters: T2's clause is that the environment REGENERATES the corpus to the registered hash 1d2319301a7b52dfe369819bc8029f7b6d64ad820d828f041eba15a91348390b. Copying the existing local corpus.npz onto the host would NOT satisfy that clause — it would demonstrate only that the environment can read a file. It would, however, be sufficient to run T5 and T6, which need the instances and the solvers rather than a regeneration proof.
options_not_chosen_by_the_developer: Provision the development dataset onto the host — a host mutation, and the dataset needs its own identity binding before it can be an input to a governed run.
Transfer the local corpus.npz — unblocks T5/T6 but leaves A-2's reproduction clause UNSATISFIED, which must then be stated in the disposition record rather than quietly treated as met.
Narrow A-2 by ruling — accept environment identity via image digest, thread env and stack provenance, and record corpus reproduction as deferred.

findings.statement: A filesystem sweep found /opt/mr002/stage/v2open/run/validation2.duckdb, which appeared to contradict the custody record's claim that the host copy was deleted. It does not. The sealed custody record MR002_ConsumedValidation2_MaterializationCustodyTransfer_v1.0 accounts for it explicitly under 'also_present_and_deliberately_retained': it is the FAILED FIRST ATTEMPT's database from 12:07:54Z, created before the resource-policy refusal, containing zero tables and no Validation-2 bytes, retained because it is the artifact behind the PreReadFailure record.

The CONSUMED materialization (13,905,920 bytes, created 14:26:22Z) is absent: both a targeted search and a whole-filesystem size-band sweep returned nothing.
